e.text: A2's podcast push leads at 14.7%, more than double the 6.2% benchmark; asking the Critic how to improve it.

e.note: Reading results for A2, A1, A3

critique.summary: A2's media-led push leads on every measure: 14.7% reach (10th percentile 12.7%) at $796 per point versus the benchmark's 6.2% at $1923, and its podcast and Nasty Gal spots are the most efficient actions tested. The zone-dense plans (A1, A3) build strong word of mouth in Lower West Side bars, but their pop-ups ($2500 each) and South Lawndale/Bridgeport ads return little, and A1 leaves Bridgeport (zone 1) unseeded.

findings.finding: Reaches 14.7% (12.7%–16.1%) at $796 per point, 2.4x the benchmark, with an even spread of 11.1–15.5% across districts; Very Really Good and Nasty Gal are each credited with 10.3% of adoption.

Reaches 11.6% (10.2%–12.8%) at $1009 per point; $300 bar partners earn 3.1–4.1% each, but the Mi Tierra pop-up (2.4% for $2500) and South Lawndale ads (1.9% for $1800) are weak, and Luxury streetwear and R&B reach only 4.1%.

Reaches 11.4% at $993 per point but has the widest spread (9.6%–13.3%); the day-36 Sakura pop-up earns 1.9% for $2500 and Bridgeport ads 1.5% for $1200, which is too late and too costly for word of mouth to compound.
Reaches 6.2% at $1923 per point; citywide broad ads carry 24.2% of adoption, while street teams add 0.0–0.9% each.

changes.change: Keep A2's two podcasts and the Nasty Gal collab, but shorten social:city to about 10 days (start day 31) and use the savings for the three best Lower West Side bar partners (Giant Penny Whistle, Green Room Tap, El Trebol at $300 each).
changes.why: Those bars earn 3.1–4.6% of adoption each for $300, which adds dense seeding in zone 0, the zone with 10.6% of the audience.

changes.change: Drop all $2500 pop-ups (Mi Tierra day 37, Sakura day 36), plus social:2 South Lawndale and social:1 Bridgeport.
changes.why: They are the weakest actions per dollar (1.5–2.4% of adoption) and the late ones leave no time for word of mouth to spread.

changes.change: Move the Very Really Good spot to day 3 and the Jenna & Julien spot to day 12 instead of day 20.
changes.why: Word of mouth drives over half of adoption, so earlier seeding gives it more time to compound before launch.

changes.change: Add one $300 Bridgeport partner in zone 1 (fit 0.764, 5.8% of the audience) early in the campaign.
changes.why: Zone 1 is a strong fit and is unseeded in both A1 and A2.

e.note: A2's media-led push leads on every measure: 14.7% reach (10th percentile 12.7%) at $796 per point versus the benchmark's 6.2% at $1923, and its podcast and Nasty Gal spots are the most efficient actions tested. The zone-dense plans (A1, A3) build strong word of mouth in Lower West Side bars, but their pop-ups ($2500 each) and South Lawndale/Bridgeport ads return little, and A1 leaves Bridgeport (zone 1) unseeded.

e.text: Revising A2 with the Critic's notes: earlier podcasts, cheap Pilsen bar partners, no $2,500 pop-ups.

e.note: Revising: Base on A2: Very Really Good day 3, Jenna & Julien day 12, keep Nasty Gal; trim citywide social to the last ~10 days; add Giant Penny Whistle, Green Room Tap, El Trebol and one Bridgeport partner ($300 each). Variant 2: same but keep citywide social longer and add La Malinche poster instead of Bridgeport.

strategies.thesis: Early host-read spots on Very Really Good (0.95) and Jenna & Julien (0.93) plus the Nasty Gal drop (0.96) reach 25–29 Latino and LGBTQ fans citywide, while $300 partners at Lower West Side bars (0.82–0.83) and One City Tap in Bridgeport keep word of mouth going in the strongest zones before a final 10-day citywide ad push.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Podcasts, Nasty Gal drop and Pilsen bars reach ~3x the benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is early host-read podcast spots and a Nasty Gal co-branded drop to reach Kali Uchis and Omar Apollo fans citywide, with four $300 neighborhood bar partners keeping word of mouth going near Thalia Hall before a 10-day social push. Qloo taste data shows this audience over-indexes strongly on Very Really Good (0.95), Jenna & Julien (0.93), Nasty Gal (0.96) and the Lower West Side and Bridgeport bars (0.82–0.83). In a simulation built on that data, the plan reaches 19.5% of the natural audience (17.2%–21.7% range), about 3.1x the 6.2% benchmark, at $609 per point of reach versus $1923, with word of mouth driving 56% of adoption; this is a projection, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: 6–5 weeks before launch
items: 42–39 days before launch: sign the four bar partners (Giant Penny Whistle, Green Room Tap, El Trebol, One City Tap), deliver posters and flyers; they run the whole campaign.
38 days before launch: host-read ad airs on Very Really Good.
36 days before launch: Nasty Gal co-branded drop goes live; runs 25 days.

weeks.label: 4–3 weeks before launch
items: 29 days before launch: host-read ad airs on Jenna & Julien Podcast.
28–21 days before launch: check bar flyers are up; add a playable track link or QR code to posters so people hear her first.

weeks.label: 2 weeks before launch
items: 14–11 days before launch: Nasty Gal drop wraps (ends 11 days before launch); refresh bar materials and plan a 21+ pre-show pop-up at Giant Penny Whistle.

weeks.label: 10 days before launch to launch week
items: 10 days before launch: start targeted social ads across Chicago, weighted to best-fit areas; run through launch day.
Launch week: pre-show gathering at Giant Penny Whistle; partners push last-call posts.

risks: Results come from a simulation on Qloo taste data; real reach may fall outside the 17.2%–21.7% range.
Three bar partners are the weakest actions (1.6–1.8% credit); they matter mainly for word of mouth, which may underperform.
South Lawndale/La Villita fans may miss it: no partner there, as a simulated voice noted.
Podcast audiences are national; Chicago share of listeners is an assumption.
measure: Weekly ticket sales tracked against podcast, Nasty Gal and bar promo codes or links.
Scans of poster QR codes at each bar partner.
Nasty Gal drop traffic and click-through to tickets.
Social ad cost per ticket click once the push starts 10 days before launch.
